analysis.title: Nomura McElligott - REPRICING THE LEFT-TAIL...FAST
key_insights: Equity vol, skew and vol-of-vol are rising on outright hedge buying after being ignored in recent weeks. Spot equities are moving through the megacap tech / Nasdaq / QQQ negative gamma flip (e.g. $715 in QQQ), and the spot/vol correlation has returned to the standard negative form (spot down, vol up).
USD rate vol is also bid alongside a Treasury risk-off rally. Large bullish trades and vol buying in 5 and 10 year futures are reported, and UST yields are at fresh one-month lows.
Treasuries are acting as an equity hedge again, and the bond/stock correlation has reversed. McElligott reads this as the market repricing the probability of a US growth scare.

Tech (-2.9%) and Energy (-1.7%) fell today. These are the two leading S&P sectors YTD and the legs of the Semis / Energy barbell, which the note says is +60% YTD on a 3 Sharpe, so McElligott calls this real de-risking.

The AI trajectory rethink started last week and continued overnight. Items cited: a weak Anthropic ARR figure and questions about its IPO viability, Gartner's negative view of CoreWeave / neocloud / infrastructure names, poorly received AI-ecosystem IPOs globally, and disappointing guidance from LRCX.

The market is also reading capex as flattening against lofty estimates, even though META raised capex and is doing a large equity secondary. McElligott takes META's secondary to mean hyperscalers are in effect selling calls on themselves.

Expectations for AI and hyperscaler profitability and the return to positive free cash flow have been reset lower. AI financing costs are increasingly non-linear, credit spreads are widening in a stressed way, and more debt, loan and equity issuance is coming.

The rethink now affects assumptions about AI capex trickling down into the US economy. That trickle-down, plus global fiscal dominance and still not-restrictive-enough policy rates, has kept US nominal GDP running at 6-10% for much of the year and supported the earnings growth backdrop.

McElligott's earlier view was that the recent UST short squeeze came from crowded short/paid positioning and PNL monetization in a drawdown-sensitive year, especially into Q4 and year-end comp season. He said then that it was not yet a macro regime capitulation into a growth scare.
His view has now shifted. He says the left side of the 2027+ US growth distribution is being repriced because of the AI rethink, and that this feeds the loop of Treasuries hedging AI-equity vol.
Overnight and morning flow was heavy in rate options, mostly paper paying for upside in TY, TYZ, TYX and FVH. In equities, there was SPX Jan 5900 put paper and VIX Nov 25 call buying.

sector_views.rationale: Tech fell 2.9% today as the AI trajectory rethink cut profitability and free cash flow expectations and raised AI financing costs. The note is a flow and positioning read, not a formal sector rating.
Energy fell 1.7% today alongside tech as part of the Semis / Energy barbell unwind. The note gives no formal rating.

earnings_insights: LRCX gave disappointing guidance, cited as one trigger of the AI trajectory rethink. The note gives no figures.
META raised capex versus prior expectations and is doing a large equity secondary. The note reads this as hyperscalers selling calls on themselves.
The note says AI/hyperscaler profitability and free cash flow expectations are being reset lower, and that a US nominal GDP running at 6-10% has supported the corporate earnings growth backdrop.

macro_indicators.reading: Running in a 6-10% band for much of the year
macro_indicators.interpretation: Hot nominal growth, driven by AI capex trickle-down, deficit spending and not-restrictive-enough policy rates, has supported the earnings growth backdrop. The AI rethink now puts those assumptions at risk.
Treasuries are working as a risk-asset hedge again, in line with repricing of a US growth scare.

risk_factors: A US growth scare. The left side of the 2027+ US growth distribution is being repriced as the AI capex trickle-down assumption weakens.
AI financing costs are increasingly non-linear, credit spreads are widening in a stressed way, and more debt, loan and equity issuance is coming.
Hyperscaler profitability and free cash flow expectations are being reset lower.
Further unwinds in the crowded Semis / Energy barbell, which is +60% YTD.
Broader rates volatility, which has come in waves since the March energy shock.
vol_and_positioning: Equity vol, skew and vol-of-vol (demand for wings) are jumping on outright hedge buying after being an afterthought in recent weeks.
The spot/vol correlation has flipped to the standard negative form (spot down, vol up).
QQQ is moving through a negative gamma flip level, e.g. $715.
USD rate vol rose across the surface, most in short expiries. 1m expiries on 1y/2y underlyings rose 10.1/11.2 vol points, while expiries beyond 5 years were flat to slightly lower.
Equity option flow: SPX Jan 5900P paper paid 18.3 on 1.3k live floor, VIX Nov 25 C bid .85 on 18,150 committed trades, and a Dec 7400P tie to 7730 25d paper bought 2k at $84.50.
Overnight UST option flow: TYX 106.5C, TYZ 108.5C (49,999), a TY wk 5 105.25/105.75 strangle paying 36 up to 37 on 20k, and a TY wk 5 106.5/108 call spread on 30k.
This morning's UST option flow: FVH 106C paid 25.5 up to 27 on 15k and 26 up to 27 on 20k, FVH 110C paid 5 on 5k, TYZ 107.5C paid 16 on 23k, and TYZ 107C paid 23 on 17k.
The earlier UST short squeeze was driven by crowded short/paid positioning and PNL monetization in a performance year focused on drawdown survival, especially into Q4 and year-end comp season.
geopolitical: The Iran / March energy shock that set off the rate vol blast is cited as the origin of the rates volatility seen this year.
The note refers to the AI Cold War as the framing for the Semis / Energy barbell, with tech and energy as its two core constraints.
